import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import io

# Prepare the dataset
csv_data = """Person ID,Gender,Age,Occupation,Sleep Duration,Quality of Sleep,Physical Activity Level,Stress Level,BMI Category,Blood Pressure,Heart Rate,Daily Steps,Sleep Disorder
1,Male,27,Software Engineer,6.1,6,42,6,Overweight,126/83,77,4200,,
2,Male,28,Doctor,6.2,6,60,8,Normal,125/80,75,10000,,
3,Male,28,Doctor,6.2,6,60,8,Normal,125/80,75,10000,,
4,Male,28,Sales Representative,5.9,4,30,8,Obese,140/90,85,3000,Sleep Apnea
5,Male,28,Sales Representative,5.9,4,30,8,Obese,140/90,85,3000,Sleep Apnea
"""

# Read the data into a pandas DataFrame
df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(csv_data))

# --- Data Preprocessing ---
# Fill missing 'Sleep Disorder' values with 'None' for clarity
df['Sleep Disorder'].fillna('None', inplace=True)
# Drop duplicate rows to simplify visualization (two doctors and two sales reps are identical)
df_unique = df.drop_duplicates().reset_index()

# --- Visualization ---
# Set a professional and modern style for the plot
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", context="talk")
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 9))

# Create a bubble chart to show multiple dimensions of the data
# X-axis: Stress Level
# Y-axis: Quality of Sleep
# Hue (color): BMI Category
# Size: Physical Activity Level
# Style (marker): Sleep Disorder
scatter = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df_unique,
    x='Stress Level',
    y='Quality of Sleep',
    hue='BMI Category',
    size='Physical Activity Level',
    style='Sleep Disorder',
    sizes=(300, 2500),  # Control the min and max size of bubbles
    palette='viridis',
    alpha=0.8,
    edgecolor='black',
    linewidth=1.5,
    ax=ax
)

# --- Annotations and Customizations ---
# Add text labels for each occupation to make the plot highly interpretable
for i in range(df_unique.shape[0]):
    plt.text(
        x=df_unique['Stress Level'][i] + 0.08,
        y=df_unique['Quality of Sleep'][i],
        s=df_unique['Occupation'][i],
        fontdict=dict(color='black', size=14, weight='bold')
    )

# Set informative title and axis labels
ax.set_title('Impact of Lifestyle Factors on Sleep Quality', fontsize=22, weight='bold', pad=20)
ax.set_xlabel('Stress Level (1-10 Scale)', fontsize=16, labelpad=15)
ax.set_ylabel('Quality of Sleep (1-10 Scale)', fontsize=16, labelpad=15)

# Adjust axis limits for better spacing and clarity
ax.set_xlim(5.5, 8.5)
ax.set_ylim(3.5, 6.8)
ax.tick_params(axis='both', which='major', labelsize=12)

# Improve the legend for clarity
# Move the legend outside the plot area
handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
# Manually reorder and title sections of the legend
bmi_index = labels.index('BMI Category')
disorder_index = labels.index('Sleep Disorder')
activity_index = labels.index('Physical Activity Level')

legend = ax.legend(
    handles[bmi_index+1:disorder_index] + handles[disorder_index+1:activity_index] + handles[activity_index+1:],
    labels[bmi_index+1:disorder_index] + labels[disorder_index+1:activity_index] + labels[activity_index+1:],
    bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1),
    loc='upper left',
    borderaxespad=0.,
    fontsize=12,
    title='Legend',
    title_fontsize=14
)

# Add titles inside the legend box
legend.get_texts()[0].set_text('BMI Category')
legend.get_texts()[0].set_weight('bold')
legend.get_texts()[3].set_text('\nSleep Disorder')
legend.get_texts()[3].set_weight('bold')
legend.get_texts()[5].set_text('\nPhysical Activity Level')
legend.get_texts()[5].set_weight('bold')


# Adjust layout to make room for the legend
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.85, 1])

# Save the resulting plot to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
